harness.note: The better-borg-c runner and observer at this commit build and run every specimen. A specimen is the game and Borg source at its own ref; the observer instrumentation comes from the harness commit. It applies to specimens of kind "better-borg-c" (the default). Specimens of kind "borg-rs" are built and run by borg-rs's own harness at the specimen's ref (harness/build.sh and the borgh frontend). This pin is also a specimen ref (4.2.6-bbc-9ca98661): the harness bumped with the mode-cutoff restart so runner and specimens move together (borg-zoo#54).

experiment.prespecified:
Fixed 2026-11-21, before any result of these builds was read (borg-zoo#571; borg-reborn-rs #814, source RULES20). Standard
classes-18 pilot (RULES 16) on the two exact specimens, shipped harness/borg.txt defaults, borg-rs core, errand none, cap
100,000; 36 games, evidence retained. Nothing is expanded automatically: the gate is returned first; an exact native45
follow-up, if required, keeps the manifest sha256 7c81c28c03be3e6c188cb555fa8c917402bae0819d0791a1a810e031214d2eed
(suite reborn-native-full45) and needs its own gate and the owner's disposition (the #520 authorization was specific to its
old two refs).
Gate: both exact builds; one binary each; every cell, build, config, effective setting and retained evidence inspected; no
config_error, stall, timeout or crash; paired key, message and state differences and full-trace evidence hashes where
retained; outcomes and final fields consistent; source, binary, config and parameter receipt pins. The ten new defaults must be
40/65/65/8/10/3/5/20/5500/3501 in the candidate (compiled defaults read from params-core.json, since the effective-settings
echo omits defaults) and absent from the baseline; the resolved-settings receipt (settings_resolved) of each cell is
kept and read. No non-neutral arm. Stop on a mismatch and report the exact start, first differing key, trace and source;
report adapter and echo limits instead of declaring strict parity silently. All failures and deaths retained and
classified. No population or survival-improvement claim.
